name: Hittites
desc: Rulers of the 'land of a thousand gods' in central Anatolia, who fought Egypt to a standstill at Kadesh and then signed the oldest peace treaty that survives. They wrote the oldest Indo-European language on record.
source: The royal archives of Hattusa (Boğazköy), excavated from 1906; the language deciphered by Bedřich Hrozný in 1915

belligerent: drove a chariot of three men through the enemy line
devout: performed the rite that sends a sickness away on a donkey
cautious: sealed the grain silo with clay before the long winter

inventions.name: Three-Man Chariot
inventions.source: Egyptian reliefs of Kadesh (1274 BCE) show Hittite chariots carrying a driver, a spearman and a shield-bearer
inventions.desc: A heavy chariot with a driver, a spearman and a shield-man: +2 attack, and everyone moves 3% faster.
inventions.hint: Needs Beast Domestication and Polished Stone Tools, in the Tribe & Agrarian Era.

inventions.name: Iron Blades
inventions.source: Hittite smiths worked iron, still rare and precious; a letter of Hattusili III to an Assyrian king says good iron is not to be had just now
inventions.desc: A few precious blades of the black metal, harder than bronze: +2 attack, +1 defence.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy, and long work at the furnace.

inventions.name: Sealed Grain Silos
inventions.source: An underground silo complex at Hattusa (16th century BCE) could hold several thousand tonnes of grain
inventions.desc: Deep chambers sealed airtight with clay keep grain for years: the stores hold 40 more food, and food spoils 8% slower.
inventions.hint: Needs pottery and the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and builders who harvest.

inventions.name: Stag Rhyton
inventions.source: Silver drinking vessels shaped as a stag or a fist, used to pour offerings to the gods
inventions.desc: A vessel shaped like a stag, for pouring wine to the thousand gods: rites bring 10% more devotion, +1 mood.

foods.name: Thick Honey Bread
foods.source: Hittite texts list dozens of kinds of offering bread; the Hittite laws set prices for beehives
foods.desc: Thick loaves sweetened with honey, for the table and the gods: hunger grows 8% slower, +1 mood.

foods.name: Libation Wine
foods.desc: Wine from the vineyards of the plateau, poured first to the gods and then to the guests: +3 mood.
foods.hint: Needs pottery, and rites at the hearth.

finds.name: Fallen Sky-Iron
finds.source: The earliest iron objects were made from meteorites; Hittite texts speak of 'iron of heaven'
finds.desc: A heavy black stone that fell burning from the sky. It is holy, and it can be hammered.

finds.name: Hazel Groves
finds.desc: Thickets of hazel under the oaks, full of nuts in autumn.

people.name: Hasusara
people.desc: Her name means 'queen', and she rules the stores like one.
memory: counted the jars in the great silo and found not one missing

people.name: Tarhunta-piya
people.desc: He breaks horses to the yoke and talks to them like brothers.
memory: drove a team of horses across the river in flood

people.name: Anitta
people.source: The Anitta Text, the oldest known text in the Hittite language
people.desc: An early king who took Hattusa, sowed weeds on its ruins and cursed whoever would settle there again. The Hittites later made it their capital.

people.name: Mursili II
people.source: The Plague Prayers of Mursili II, late 14th century BCE
people.desc: A king who searched the old tablets for the sin that brought twenty years of plague, and confessed his father's broken oath to the gods.

people.name: Tawagalawa
people.source: The Tawagalawa letter, c. 1250 BCE, names him as the brother of the king of Ahhiyawa, probably a Mycenaean Greek
people.text: a lord from across the western sea, who arrives in a chariot and speaks the court tongue with a strange accent.
memory: crossed the sea with ships full of bronze and wine
people.desc: A Mycenaean lord, perhaps called Eteocles in Greek, who appears in Hittite letters.

people.name: Suppiluliuma
people.label: Suppiluliuma the Great King
people.desc: He makes the Hittites an empire. Combat 8, 85 HP.

people.name: Puduhepa
people.label: Puduhepa the Priestess Queen
people.desc: A queen who sealed treaties and wrote to the queen of Egypt. Lore 7, Trade 4.

people.name: Hattusili
people.label: Hattusili the Peacemaker
people.desc: He signs an eternal peace with Egypt. Combat 5, Lore 5, Crafting 5.

events.title: The Plague That Will Not Leave
events.source: Mursili II blamed a twenty-year plague on prisoners brought from Egypt and on his father's broken oath
events.text: Death keeps visiting the huts. The diviners say an old oath was broken and the gods are angry. The chief must decide what to do.

options.label: Confess and make amends
options.result: The chief stands before the gods and names the wrong. Gifts are sent to those who were wronged. The sickness slackens.

options.label: Send the sickness away on a donkey
options.result: A donkey decked with ribbons is driven toward the enemy's land, carrying the plague with it.

options.label: Keep the sick apart
options.result: The sick are carried to huts outside the camp. It is hard, but fewer fall ill.

events.title: An Eternal Peace
events.source: The treaty between Hattusili III and Ramesses II (c. 1259 BCE), written in Akkadian on silver tablets; a copy hangs at the United Nations
events.text: After years of raids back and forth, the rival chief sends word: let us swear peace forever, return each other's runaways, and help each other against any enemy.

options.label: Swear the peace
options.result: The oath is cut into a tablet of silver and set before the gods of both peoples.

options.label: Fight on
options.result: The envoy is sent home. The raids go on.

events.title: A Thousand Gods
events.source: The Hittites welcomed the gods of every land they met into their own pantheon, and called themselves the land of a thousand gods
events.text: The newcomers have brought their own gods with them. Instead of throwing them out, the priests give them a place in the shrine beside ours, and a share of the offerings.

tales.name: The God Who Went Away
tales.text: Telipinu flew into a rage, put his left shoe on his right foot, and walked away into the steppe. Mist filled the windows, the barley stopped growing, cows and sheep turned away their young. Even the gods went hungry. At last a little bee found him asleep in a meadow and stung him awake, and the healers soothed his anger.

tales.name: The Storm God and the Serpent
tales.source: The Illuyanka myth, recited at the spring festival of Purulli
tales.text: The serpent Illuyanka beat the Storm God. So the goddess Inara laid out a great feast, and the serpent and its children ate and drank until they could not crawl back into their hole. Then a mortal tied the serpent with a rope, and the Storm God came and killed it.

tales.name: The Stone Giant Ullikummi
tales.source: The Song of Ullikummi, a Hurrian myth in Hittite
tales.text: The old god Kumarbi made a son of stone to overthrow the Storm God. Planted on a giant's shoulder in the sea, it grew until it reached the sky. No weapon could hurt it, until the wise god Ea took the ancient copper knife that once cut heaven from earth, and cut the stone giant from the shoulder it stood on.
tales.moral: find the root of a problem

tales.name: The Purulli Festival
tales.source: Purulli, the spring festival at Nerik, when the year was renewed
tales.text: When the earth wakes, the king and queen travel to the holy city. The old story of the serpent is told again, the races are run, and the gods are given new bread and wine, so that the land may live another year.
